title: Qwen-Audio-3.1 goes multilingual: ASR now covers 59 languages and 8 Chinese dialects
summary: Want AI to understand your hometown dialect — or speak it back? Qwen has rolled out a multilingual upgrade for the three speech models in its Qwen-Audio-3.1 family, with the emphasis on Chinese dialects.
ai_summary: On November 26, Qwen announced multilingual capabilities for the Qwen-Audio-3.1 family, with a focus on Chinese dialects. The upgrade spans three product tracks: speech recognition (ASR, speech to text) supports 59 languages and 8 Chinese dialects; speech synthesis (TTS, text to speech) supports 65 languages and 6 Chinese dialects; and Realtime (live voice, back-and-forth conversation) supports 53 languages and 6 Chinese dialects. For teams building customer service, subtitles, voiceover, or voice assistants, this adds a ready-made multilingual/dialect entry point — especially useful for serving users who speak different dialects. One caveat: the numbers come from Qwen's announcement, and the post does not say which dialects are covered or provide benchmark results, so validate with real audio before deploying.
brief: ASR (speech recognition) now supports 59 languages and 8 Chinese dialects.
TTS (text-to-speech) supports 65 languages and 6 Chinese dialects — the widest language coverage of the three.
Realtime (live speech) supports 53 languages and 6 Chinese dialects.
All three models are available through Qwen's official channels, and each can be tried separately.

sections.h: What this is: a multilingual upgrade for Qwen-Audio-3.1's three speech models

blocks.p: Qwen-Audio-3.1 is Qwen's previously released family of speech foundation models. On November 26, the company announced multilingual capabilities for the family, with a strong focus on Chinese dialects. Think of a speech foundation model as the base layer for voice applications: recognition, synthesis, and real-time conversation each get their own track.

ASR (automatic speech recognition) turns audio into text; TTS (text-to-speech) turns text into audio; and Realtime is live speech for back-and-forth conversation. Qwen says this update strengthens Chinese dialect support in both recognition and synthesis.

sections.h: How many languages and dialects does each model cover?

blocks.p: Qwen gives three sets of numbers. By language count, TTS covers the most, ASR comes next, and Realtime covers the fewest. For Chinese dialects, ASR covers two more than the other two.

blocks.p: These figures come from Qwen's announcement and reflect the vendor's own numbers. The post includes no third-party evaluations, and the totals don't mean every language or dialect performs equally well.

sections.h: Why the focus on Chinese dialects?

blocks.p: Dialects are a real challenge for speech models: the same meaning can sound very different across dialects, many dialects lack a standardized written form, and training data is relatively scarce. Qwen frames the headline of this update as "enhanced Chinese dialect recognition and synthesis" — both dialect recognition and synthesis are stronger, and the improvement spans all three product tracks.

But the post gives only the number of dialects, not which ones. The charts below show Chinese dialects as a share of each model's total language count, making clear that dialects are a small slice of the whole.

blocks.p: The post doesn't provide any of this; you'll need to verify it yourself before deployment or wait for Qwen's follow-up.

The value is clear: if your product serves users across multiple languages or dialects, these three tracks give you ready-made entry points — ASR for transcription, TTS for voice synthesis and narration, and Realtime for live conversation.
The trade-off is that, for now, there are only Qwen's own counts and no public benchmarks, pricing, or specific dialect list — so you shouldn't launch based on the numbers alone.

list: If you're building multilingual subtitles or customer-service transcription, start with ASR.
If you need audiobooks, voiceover, or multilingual announcements, look at TTS.
If you're building a voice assistant or real-time translation, look at Realtime.
If your users speak a specific dialect, first confirm it's on the list of 8 or 6 dialects.

main.title: New multilingual capabilities are here for Qwen-Audio-3.1! Especially for Chinese dialects.
